resources.string: YouTube and Twitch ads and promoted posts on social networks come from the same servers as the content, so no blocker of this kind can remove them. An empty gap may remain where an ad was on websites: for that, use Brave or Firefox with uBlock Origin; they complement Garbillo.

If something fails (the app closes, a list doesn\'t download, an update doesn\'t install…), Garbillo can send an anonymous report so we can fix it. It includes the type of failure, where in the code it happened, the Garbillo and Android versions, the phone brand and the blocking level.

It never includes websites, history, your apps, your network, any phone identifier or the error text. Your IP isn\'t stored. It\'s sent at most once a day and, if you choose \"Wi-Fi only\", only over Wi-Fi. You can see the exact report before it\'s sent and turn it off whenever you want.
Blocks ads, trackers and dangerous websites
Across the whole phone: in the browser and inside apps, without root.
Uses a local VPN, not an external server
The \"VPN\" lives inside your phone and only looks at which domain each app wants to connect to. It doesn\'t see what you do and your browsing never leaves the phone.
You\'ll see a key and a persistent notification
Android always shows them while a VPN is active. It\'s normal and doesn\'t drain the battery. The first time you turn on the filter, Android will ask for permission (\"Connection request\").
Which apps do you want to protect?
You can change this anytime in Settings → Protected apps.
Some system settings can turn the filter off without warning. Each step is optional and you can do it later from Settings → Battery and startup.
Lists (5 to 40 MB) and checks run automatically when you connect to Wi-Fi. Anything you request manually always downloads.
To alert you about blocked dangerous websites and new versions.
So power saving doesn\'t close the filter. Garbillo barely uses battery: it sleeps until a query arrives. Find Garbillo and choose \"Don\'t optimize\" or \"Unrestricted\".
This phone needs it for the filter to come back on its own after restarting or updating. %1$s
All except the ones I choose
Everything is filtered except the apps you select.
Only the apps you select are filtered.
Every new change as soon as it\'s made, before it becomes stable. For trying the latest; may break.
Maximum compatibility. Very low risk of anything breaking.
For everyday use: set it and forget it. Blocks well without breaking anything common.
Aggressive privacy. May break some app or link.
Blocks encrypted DNS servers so browsers and apps can\'t bypass the filter.
Ads in free games and apps (GoodbyeAds list). May break some rewards for watching ads.
Light alternative focused on ads and tracking.
Ads and tracking from your %1$s phone\'s own system.
Recommended for phones: the most active threats. About 10 MB of memory.
All known threats (more than a million domains). About 40 MB of memory: only for phones with plenty of memory.
Swiss non-profit foundation. No logs with your IP; also blocks malware domains.
The fastest in most places. Deletes logs within 24 hours.
Swedish VPN company focused on privacy. No logs, no filtering of its own.
Internal rule (turns off Firefox\'s encrypted DNS)
Garbillo does not answer their DNS queries, so almost all of them lose their connection. An app that connects straight to an IP address could still have internet.
Check the apps that must not connect to the internet while Garbillo is on. They always go through the filter, even if you excluded them.
If you cut off their internet, they will stop working.
Off: nothing is recorded or sent.
Only this domain, the reason and the note are sent. It helps improve the lists for everyone. Nothing from your history or your apps.

Android has \"Block connections without VPN\" turned on. Garbillo only filters DNS and doesn\'t carry the rest of the traffic, so with that option Android cuts off all internet. Tap the gear next to Garbillo and turn it off; you can keep \"Always-on VPN\".
With a fixed private DNS provider, Android bypasses the filter. Go to Settings → Network → Private DNS and choose \"Automatic\" or \"Off\".
Your private DNS (%1$s) is on the block lists, so Android can\'t use it and the phone has no internet. Go to Settings → Network → Private DNS and choose \"Automatic\" or \"Off\".
The lists were already up to date
You\'re using mobile data or a metered Wi-Fi. Downloading the lists can take 5 to 40 MB depending on which ones you have on (almost nothing if they\'re already up to date).
An Android setting is cutting off the connection (see the notice below)
Android\'s private DNS bypasses the filter (see the notice below)
Android\'s private DNS is blocked and cuts off the connection (see the notice below)
The lists will download as soon as you connect to an unmetered Wi-Fi. If you don\'t want to wait, tap \"Update now\" (it will use the current network).
No list is loaded. Check the connection and tap \"Update now\".
The filter is on, but the network\'s DNS isn\'t responding. Is there an internet connection?
Couldn\'t turn on the VPN. Is another VPN active?
History is off. You can turn it on in Settings.

%1$s is on the threat list (phishing, malware or scams). If you allow it, Garbillo will stop protecting you from it in every app. Only do it if you\'re sure the list is wrong; otherwise, better report it.
It\'s on the threat list (phishing, malware or scams). Only allow it if you\'re sure it\'s trustworthy.
No longer on any active list
Remember: Android keeps answers for a few minutes. If an app still doesn\'t work after allowing a domain, close it and open it again.
You have the latest version of the %1$s channel.
Allow Garbillo to install updates and tap \"Install\" again.

Installing… Android will ask you to confirm. If Google Play Protect blocks it or warns that the app is unknown, tap \"More details\" → \"Install anyway\": it appears because Garbillo isn\'t on Google Play.
To go back to Stable from a newer version, you\'ll have to wait for a higher stable release (Android doesn\'t allow installing an older version).
Important: your version has a security issue fixed in this one. Install it as soon as possible.
It checks only once a day and notifies you. Nothing is ever installed without your confirmation.
The published version can\'t be found on GitHub. Try again later.
The download doesn\'t match the published one (different fingerprint).
The download isn\'t Garbillo or isn\'t signed with its key.
Couldn\'t update: the installed version is signed with a different key. Uninstall it once and install the one from GitHub.

Android blocked the update. If it was Google Play Protect, try again and, in its warning, tap \"More details\" → \"Install anyway\". If the phone is managed by a company or school, it may not allow installing apps from outside Google Play.
Fixes a security issue in your version. Tap to install it.
Tap to see what\'s new and install it.
Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → \"Never sleeping apps\" → add Garbillo.
Xiaomi: Settings → Apps → Garbillo → Battery saver → \"No restrictions\".
OPPO/Realme/OnePlus: Settings → Battery → Garbillo → allow background activity.
Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Garbillo → turn on \"Autostart\".
Settings → Battery → App launch → Garbillo → \"Manage manually\" and turn on all three options.
Settings → Apps → Garbillo → turn on \"Auto launch\" (or \"Allow auto launch\").
Settings → Battery → Background power consumption → Garbillo, and in i Manager → Autostart → Garbillo.
On this phone, the system won\'t let Garbillo turn itself back on after restarting or updating unless it has \"Autostart\" permission.
Don\'t let Android close the filter

System battery saving can close the filter when you\'re not using the phone. Garbillo barely uses battery (it sleeps until a query arrives), so it\'s safe to exclude it: find Garbillo in the list and choose \"Don\'t optimize\" or \"Unrestricted\".
Android didn\'t let it turn on when the phone started. Tap to turn it on.
No internet because of an Android setting
\"Block connections without VPN\" is on, and with Garbillo that cuts off all internet. Tap, open Garbillo\'s gear and turn that option off (keep \"Always-on VPN\").
Alert when a phishing, malware or scam site is blocked.
%1$s is on the threat list (phishing, malware or scams) and has been blocked. Requested by: %2$s. If you weren\'t expecting it, there\'s nothing you need to do.
Unlock your phone to see the details.
The filter keeps working with the lists you already have.
The filter keeps working with the lists you already have. It will try again automatically; you can also tap \"Update now\".
There\'s no error pending to be sent.
Not enough memory to load all the lists; the previous ones are kept.
Select the apps you want to leave out of the filter. Everything else is filtered.
Select the apps you want to filter. Everything else is left alone.
Recommended to exclude them: some don\'t work with an active VPN.
Filtering them isn\'t recommended: some don\'t work with an active VPN.
Which website did it appear on?

Garbillo only sees the domain name, not the page. These are the websites %1$s opened around that time. The one you choose will load letting only %2$s through, and whatever it loads will be outlined in red.
%1$s isn\'t a browser: ads inside an app are drawn by the app itself and can\'t be reproduced here. You can still try with the service\'s website.
No nearby websites in the history (Android may have reused cached answers). Type the address of the website where you saw it.
The preview doesn\'t use your browser session or its cookies, and deletes everything when closed. It uses data like opening the website normally.

Couldn\'t download the list. Check the connection and try again: it was left as it was.
How much do you want to block?

Blocks known phishing domains (sites that imitate your bank, the post office or a shop to steal your data), malware, scams, fake websites and cryptomining. It works in every app: browser, email, messaging, SMS with links…
No threat has been blocked in the last %1$s.
Threats blocked in the last %1$s: %2$d. See them in History → Threats.
Alert me when a dangerous site is blocked
A block is silent: the website simply doesn\'t load. The alert tells you what was blocked and which app requested it. At most one alert per minute.

Hagezi\'s public \"Threat Intelligence Feeds\" lists, which combine dozens of security sources and are updated several times a day. The app downloads them directly from GitHub and checks them on the phone: it doesn\'t send the websites you visit to anyone. The fake-website and malicious-popup lists are already included in the Balanced blocking level.
No list is perfect: a newly created phishing site can take a few hours to appear. Be wary anyway of links that urgently ask for data or payments.
Lists added on top of the blocking level\'s list. The more you turn on, the more is blocked and the more memory the app uses.
Which apps go through the filter
Restore recommended (all except banking and payments)
You can also allow or block a domain from the history by tapping an entry.
Domains that are never blocked, even if they\'re on a list. Includes their subdomains.
Domains you always want to block. Includes their subdomains.
Something is only downloaded if the list has changed, and never with low battery.

Automatic downloads (lists, new versions and error reports) wait for Wi-Fi and run on their own as soon as you connect. Lists take 5 to 40 MB depending on which you turn on. Anything you request manually (\"Update now\") always downloads.
No automatic check has been done yet.
Only on this phone. It\'s deleted automatically after the chosen time.

Normally, the queries Garbillo lets through go unencrypted to your network\'s DNS (your carrier\'s or your router\'s), which can see them. With encrypted DNS they go over TLS to a trusted service: nobody on the network can see or change which websites you visit.
As always. Works on any network.

On a Wi-Fi with a login page (hotels, airports) the network\'s DNS is used until you sign in. If a network blocks encrypted DNS, Garbillo will warn that DNS isn\'t responding: choose another service or turn it off on that network.

Right now Android may close Garbillo to save battery. Garbillo barely uses battery (it sleeps until a query arrives), so it\'s safe to exclude it: find Garbillo and choose \"Don\'t optimize\" or \"Unrestricted\".
Garbillo is already excluded from battery saving. The filter will stay on even when you\'re not using the phone.
If you leave the filter on, Garbillo turns itself back on when the phone starts (after the first unlock) and after updating. If you still find it off, it turns on again when you open the app.
This phone also needs the \"Autostart\" permission: %1$s
On: Android starts the filter as soon as the phone turns on and reopens it if it closes.
Not on. With it, Android starts the filter as soon as the phone turns on and reopens it if something closes it.
With it, Android starts the filter as soon as the phone turns on and reopens it if something closes it.

In Android Settings → Network → VPN, tap the gear next to Garbillo and turn on \"Always-on VPN\". Don\'t turn on \"Block connections without VPN\": Garbillo only carries DNS, so with that option Android cuts off all internet on the phone.
This phone has a work profile, a Private space or a secure folder. Android gives each profile its own VPN, so Garbillo doesn\'t filter that profile\'s apps, only this one\'s.
In 24-hour tests the filter used between 0.1% and 0.4% of the battery per day.

Free games and apps, ads from the phone\'s own system and trackers in every app. To see what was blocked and decide whether you wanted it, use the history: \"View on the web\" shows you what that domain puts on the page.

Garbillo is an ad and tracker blocker for the whole phone, without root. It works inside the phone: your browsing isn\'t sent to any server and it doesn\'t collect statistics. Only what you decide to report leaves the phone.
Free software, GPLv3 license. Block lists by Hagezi and other authors.
Garbillo uses your phone\'s language. If it isn\'t available, it\'s shown in English.
